answer: Cap influence with scarce, non-stackable plots: each epoch a public garden auctions a hard cap of deeds, and only a deed-holder may vote or grade. A bidder locks a deposit set to last epoch's median reward, paid in saffron credits, and attaches a unique work artifact. Current orchard holders may challenge near-duplicates for 24 hours; a successful challenge burns the deposit and voids the deed. An attacker who wants N fake seats must win N auctions, post N deposits, and produce N distinguishable artifacts, so clone floods cost linear capital plus mass burns when outputs collide.
